# Subfield generated by a subset over a base field

Let $E$ be a field extension of a field $F$, given by an embedding $F \to E$ through which $F$ is identified with a subfield of $E$, and let $S \subseteq E$. The *subfield of $E$ generated by $S$ over $F$*, written $F(S)$, is the intersection of all subfields of $E$ that contain both $F$ and $S$. It is the smallest subfield of $E$ containing $F$ and $S$, so it is an intermediate field of the extension. When $S = \{\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_n\}$ is finite, $F(S)$ is written $F(\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_n)$.

## Sources

- David S. Dummit and Richard M. Foote, Abstract Algebra, 3rd ed., John Wiley & Sons, 2004, §13.1, pp. 516–517.
- The Stacks Project Authors, *The Stacks Project*, Definition 9.6.6, Tag 09FZ, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09FZ.
